subject: Clarify runtime-relay subprocessor scope & egress mapping for FinTrust pilot
messages:
From: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@fintrust.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps FinTrust <legalops@fintrust.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify runtime-relay subcontractors for pilot

Hi Vivek,

As part of our security intake for the pilot next month, Legal asked for a concise list of any subprocessors involved in the "runtime relay" (the lightweight proxy that routes telemetry and traces from our integration). Specifically we need:
- the current roster of subprocessors and their roles (ingest, telemetry, CDN, ops)
- whether any of these subprocessors can see PII in transit or at rest
- the egress destinations/countries for telemetry (and whether data is persisted)

Can you share an export of your runtime-relay subprocessor roster and a simple egress map? PDF or CSV is fine. Legal would like to confirm DPA coverage before we flip the switch.

Thanks,
Jacob
Jacob Reed
Security Program Manager | FinTrust
[attachment: fintrust_questionnaire_v1.docx]
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@fintrust.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify runtime-relay subcontractors for pilot

Jacob —

Thanks for the clear ask. We're pulling a focused export now. Quick summary up front:
- Short roster attached: runtime-relay-subprocessors.csv (lists role, country, DPA appendix reference)
- Two partners handle transit-only telemetry: SaaSproxy Inc. (ingest/route; no persistent logs by default) and CacheFront (CDN edge for metric scraping; retains metrics for 7 days)
- Neither partner has access to customer prompts or stored user content; telemetry relates to telemetry IDs, sampling traces, and anonymized latency histograms.

Outstanding clarifications we need from you to be definitive:
1) PII definition scope for this pilot — are connection IPs considered personal data under your classification?
2) Any on-prem/offline requirements that prevent caching at edges?

I'll attach the CSV and an annotated egress map PDF in a follow-up.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@fintrust.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify runtime-relay subcontractors for pilot

Jacob — 

Attaching the detailed export as requested (runtime-relay-subprocessors.csv) and a quick annotated map (egress-map-annotated.pdf). Highlights:
- SaaSproxy Inc. (us-east-1) — role: routing + TLS termination for telemetry; no plaintext persist by default; has SOC2 type II; covered under Appendix 2 of our DPA (link in CSV).
- CacheFront (edge vendor, multi-region) — role: short-term metric caching; retains aggregated metrics for 7 days, no user content.
- OpsAssist (managed ops) — limited access to aggregated alerts and anonymized trace IDs for on-call debugging; with JIT access logged in our audit trail.

I've also noted per-vendor egress countries in the CSV. If you treat IP addresses as PII we can enable IP hashing prior to transit (adds minimal latency).

Attachments: runtime-relay-subprocessors.csv; egress-map-annotated.pdf

Kimberly Park
Sr. Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@fintrust.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps FinTrust <legalops@fintrust.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify runtime-relay subcontractors for pilot

Thanks Kimberly — received the attachments and quick read-through looks good. A couple of follow-ups from Legal and our infra team:
- Can you confirm whether SaaSproxy writes any logs that contain full request headers (they could contain authentication bearer tokens if misconfigured)?
- For CacheFront: are metrics stored in a vendor-managed bucket that could be subject to cross-border replication? If so, where is the primary copy stored?

Legal asks for a short paragraph we can attach to the DPA addendum that states the operational constraints (retention, types of telemetry, and whether any vendor may access request payloads). Could you draft that? If helpful we can share a template.

Jacob
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@fintrust.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify runtime-relay subcontractors for pilot

Jacob —

Appended below is the short operational paragraph we can attach to your DPA addendum. We kept it intentionally concise for Legal review; happy to expand if you need more detail.

"Operational constraints for runtime relay: Redwood Inference uses a limited set of third-party subprocessors to route and temporarily cache telemetry necessary for operational observability. Subprocessors (SaaSproxy Inc., CacheFront, OpsAssist) receive only anonymized telemetry identifiers, sampling traces, and aggregated metrics; they do not receive customer request bodies, prompts, or stored user content. Retention is limited to aggregated metrics for up to 7 days (CacheFront) and transient routing logs for up to 72 hours (SaaSproxy Inc.) unless required for incident response; any access to detailed troubleshooting logs requires JIT approval and is fully audited. Documentation of subprocessor roles and DPA appendices is attached."

We also confirm: SaaSproxy does not persist full request headers by default; they keep transient TLS session metadata for 72 hours and have SOC2 controls. CacheFront's primary metric store is in us-east-1; cross-region replication is disabled for pilot accounts by default.

Attaching: runtime-relay-subprocessors.csv; egress-map-annotated.pdf

Next steps: Jacob, if Legal is happy with the paragraph we can add it as an addendum. If they want explicit IP-hashing enabled, Kim can flip the toggle in staging and share a brief note.

— Marissa
Director, Technical Program Management | Redwood Inference
